name: Q3Map2, Auto-Pigeon build 2.5.17n-ap.3030 (Quake III, experimental)
summary: Experimental: the Auto-Pigeon fork's build of the Quake III compiler q3map2, downloaded from its GitHub releases.
description:
This profile describes the Auto-Pigeon fork of q3map2 — NetRadiant-custom's Quake III map compiler — as published on the fork's GitHub releases page. It is not an upstream release, and upstream has not reviewed or accepted the fork's changes. Only the `q3map2` command-line program is built and released; the NetRadiant editor is not part of it.

Release 2.5.17n-ap.3030 is upstream `master` 8216133 (2026-09-01) plus seven compiler changes, each with a regression case of its own in the fork that fails without it: a thin brush fragment of any positive volume is kept, so thin rods and walls keep their collision; a face crossing a split plane by between 0.1 and 0.2 units is clipped instead of sent whole to one side, which filled room air; a face nearly parallel to a neighbouring face, which the compiler treats as lying on that face's plane, is still drawn when the 1/8-unit vertex snap would have put its triangles into the solid behind; a brush whose section by a split plane is smaller than 0.2 units is split instead of sent whole to one side, so a thin rod crossing a split keeps both parts; a brush whose face the compiler treated as lying on a split plane is kept on its own side of that plane, where a sliver split off by the vertex snap filled a whole pipe bore; a narrow real opening keeps its portals (upstream dropped every portal with fewer than three edges longer than 0.2 units, so a slot 0.125 wide through a wall was reported sealed, a slot reached from a room was filled and a room behind a narrow passage was not drawn); and the 1024-unit block split no longer swallows the two faces of a slot centred on it. Four more changes fix the macOS build, an out-of-bounds read and a null reference in lighting; they change no output. The program prints `2.5.17n-ap.3030+gca2e281d.upstream.82161339` on its first line and after `Q3Map (ydnar) - v`, and the check on this profile shows it, so you can see which release you pointed it at.

Release 2.5.17n-ap.3017 is refused: it reads outside a plane table for a degenerate brush side (found by AddressSanitizer after it was published). Releases 2.5.17n-ap.3020 and 2.5.17n-ap.3026 are not refused, but they close the narrow openings above (3020 also lacks the three changes before them); use 2.5.17n-ap.3030 or newer from the same page.

Known limits, held by the fork's own tests: an opening whose two faces lie within 0.1 units of each other (inside the precision every stage of the compiler treats as one plane) is still closed, so a slot 0.0625 wide is reported sealed although its source leaks; an opening wider than that stays open wherever it lies. Material within 0.1 units of a split plane may read as air at a single point, as upstream's does; the player's collision still uses the whole brush.

The archive unpacks to one folder holding `bin/`, `licenses/`, `README.md`, `build-info.json` and `MANIFEST.json`. `q3map2` is in `bin/`, beside every library it loads, so choose the unpacked folder itself — the one that contains `bin/` — not `bin/`. Each release also publishes `SHA256SUMS` and a `release-manifest.json`; check the archive against them before unpacking. The Companion downloads nothing: you fetch the archive, and this profile runs what you unpacked.

This is a second profile beside the built-in Q3Map2 one, not a replacement for it. The built-in Quake III build profiles keep naming the upstream compiler, so nothing you already build changes. To build with this one, duplicate a build profile in Profiles and choose this tool for its stages. To test maps for leaks with it, choose the built-in pipeline “Quake III — leak test, Auto-Pigeon q3map2 build” when the Companion asks which pipeline tests Quake III maps (or under Change pipeline): it runs this tool's BSP stage only, with nothing to retarget.

The actions, options and file names are the built-in Q3Map2 profile's own: the fork changes no command-line switch. Quake III remains work in progress.

license.name: GNU General Public License v2.0 or later
license.notice: The Auto-Pigeon build of q3map2 is a fork of somebody else's program, under that program's own licence, and describing it here changes nothing about that. q3map2's source files carry the GtkRadiant header — 'either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version' — so GPL-2.0-or-later is what it is conveyed under. The archive's `licenses/` folder carries the licence texts and the notice of every library in `bin/`; the corresponding source for exactly this release is the fork's tag named above, and each release also publishes a source archive. Auto-Pigeon Companion is MIT and separate: it runs this program as a separate process and does not contain, link or relicense it.

platforms.note: release 2.5.17n-ap.3030 passed the fork's CI acceptance; on 2026-10-24 it built and leak-tested the Quake III controls through this profile on Linux. Needs glibc 2.38+

acquisition.title: Use the release you downloaded
acquisition.hint: choose the unpacked auto-pigeon-q3map2 folder — the one that contains bin/, not bin/ itself
acquisition.note: Download the archive for your platform from https://github.com/auto-pigeon/q3map2/releases/tag/auto-pigeon-q3map2-v2.5.17n-ap.3030, check it against the SHA256SUMS published beside it, and unpack it into a folder of its own. Release 2.5.17n-ap.3030, SHA-256 of each archive: auto-pigeon-q3map2-2.5.17n-ap.3030-linux-amd64.zip 068666b5a9e99ba1fa18c934ae6c91c65e83e24f246f0c6ad8d0f1725c5d420e; auto-pigeon-q3map2-2.5.17n-ap.3030-windows-amd64.zip 331cec7b774db7fc5105b907d5e09c3a6c5850798fd8f7fc872447865b371042; auto-pigeon-q3map2-2.5.17n-ap.3030-macos-amd64.zip dd5545a560d01ebde4ed01c7d8059a041f8ee0a8c1a2d34afa9f988b749b0d22; auto-pigeon-q3map2-2.5.17n-ap.3030-macos-arm64.zip 005660b0dd3e5afcf22936ad317a1482d76da16e19253f20d2c1890a4a7a274c; auto-pigeon-q3map2-2.5.17n-ap.3030-linux-arm64.zip de987e416efd6cdc3701a7300a2350610546a165ef5ee31d89e7b0a4ce4f3dd8. A SHA-256 shows the download is intact; these builds are not signed. You are the authority for what you pointed at: the check says which release it is.

acquisition.title: Find it on PATH
acquisition.note: Whatever version is first on PATH. Run the version check afterwards: only the Auto-Pigeon build prints `-ap.` and `.upstream.` in its version, and a q3map2 lifted out of its folder without the libraries beside it does not start.

refuse.reason: release 2.5.17n-ap.3017 reads outside a plane table for a degenerate brush side; unpack 2.5.17n-ap.3030 or newer from the same page and choose its folder

capabilities.title: Compile a Quake III map into a BSP
capabilities.description: Reads .map source and writes the Quake III BSP, the portal file the vis stage needs, and the surface file the light stage refuses to run without. A leaked map produces a .lin line file instead of a BSP.

capabilities.title: Compute the potentially visible set
capabilities.description: Rewrites the BSP with its visibility data. Quake III has no hearability pass — that is Quake II's.

capabilities.title: Compute lighting
capabilities.description: Writes the lightmaps into the BSP. It needs the surface file and the map source beside it, both measured, and it writes no separate lighting file.

actions.title: Compile the map
actions.description:
The BSP stage. `-meta` is on by default because upstream's own help says `ALWAYS USE THIS`: without it adjacent triangles of one texture are never combined and the map is slower everywhere.

The BSP, the portal file and the surface file all appear beside the staged map source, which is why none of them declares a path.

options.name: meta
options.title: Combine adjacent surfaces
options.description: Upstream's help says of `-meta`: ALWAYS USE THIS. Turn it off only to reproduce an old build.

options.name: leaktest
options.title: Stop if the map leaks
options.description: Q3Map2 writes the `.lin` line file either way and, with this on, writes no BSP. It still exits 0 — the missing BSP is what fails the job, and the `.lin` is what you load in the editor to find the hole.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: A NAME, not a path: `-fs_game missionpack` looks for `missionpack` inside each basepath. Leave it empty for a plain base game map.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: The BSP stage was measured to produce the same file at any thread count. The lighting stage was not; see its own option.

options.name: patchmeta
options.title: Turn patches into triangle meshes
options.description: Patches are curved surfaces. This is Q3Map2's own switch, and what it does to a map with patches in it has not been measured here.

options.name: custinfoparms
options.title: Read scripts/custinfoparms.txt
options.description: Loads custom surface and content flags a mod defines. Off unless your content root has that file.

options.name: samplesize
options.title: Lightmap resolution
options.description: In units per luxel — smaller is finer and slower. Leave unset for Q3Map2's own default.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 printed `leaked`: either its flood reached an entity from outside (a line names it, and a `.lin` was written), or nothing stood in open space and it tested nothing.
diagnostics.hint: Measured: with no entity in open space — none in the map, or every one inside a solid brush — Q3Map2 prints this same banner, names no entity and writes no `.lin`. That run tested nothing and found no hole. When an entity is named, load the `.lin` in your editor: it runs from outside the map to that entity.

diagnostics.message: An entity stands inside a solid brush. Q3Map2 does not start its flood from it.
diagnostics.hint: When every entity is inside a brush the map is not tested for leaks at all, and Q3Map2 still prints `leaked`.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 stopped at its `leaked` banner rather than write a BSP — and it still exited 0, so the missing BSP is what fails this build.
diagnostics.hint: Turn the leak test off if you want the BSP anyway; it will have no usable visibility.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 named the entity and brush the leak was traced from.
A shader the map names has no image Q3Map2 could find: nothing defines it, or its script names images that are not there. A nodraw shader never warns.
diagnostics.hint: Measured: with no script the shader compiles with default surfaceparms; with a script, the script's surfaceparms still apply. In a .map the face name has no `textures/` prefix; Q3Map2 adds it, so `textures/textures/…` in this line means the prefix was written twice. Otherwise: check what the base game data and content roots are bound to, and whether the shader's `qer_editorimage` names a file that exists — an absent editor image warns even when the stage image is there. This is a warning and the BSP is still written, so the build is not a complete result.

diagnostics.message: A shader script was read out of the bound content.
A model an entity names could not be opened. Q3Map2 dropped it, wrote the BSP and exited 0, so this line is what fails the stage.
diagnostics.hint: Measured with a `misc_model` naming a file that is not there: `ERROR: Unable to open file "models/…"`, then the BSP, portal and surface files, exit status 0. A BSP missing geometry the map asked for is not the map, so the build stops here rather than carrying it into the visibility and lighting stages. Put the model where the name says — in the content folder, the base game data or a PK3 in either — or remove the entity; `companion package preview --map <your map>` lists every model a map names and where each was found.

diagnostics.message: A model an entity names is there and is not a readable MD3. Q3Map2 dropped it, wrote the BSP and exited 0, so this line is what fails the stage.
diagnostics.hint: Measured: a file with the wrong magic is `ERROR: Invalid MD3 file: Magic bytes not found`, and one whose header points outside the file is `ERROR: Invalid MD3 header: some offsets are outside the file`; both write the BSP without the model and exit 0. Export the model again, or check that the copy in the content folder or the package is whole.

diagnostics.match: ERROR: MD3 File is too small
diagnostics.message: A model an entity names is cut short: the file is smaller than an MD3 header. Q3Map2 dropped it, wrote the BSP and exited 0, so this line is what fails the stage.
diagnostics.hint: Measured with a model truncated to a few bytes. A copy that stopped early or a download that was interrupted looks like this; replace the file.

diagnostics.message: The BSP has no portals, so there is nothing for the visibility stage to compute.
Q3Map2 could not read an image the map names (an entity's `alphamap` or `_indexmap`). It reads it from the game data only: put it under the game directory, not beside the map.
diagnostics.hint: Measured on Q3Map2 2.5.17n: it looks for that name in the game data only — at `<game directory>/<name>` in your game folder or your content folder (`baseq3/<name>` for a plain base-game map), or inside a `.pk3` that is directly in that game directory. It does not look beside the map, in its working directory, or in an archive kept in a subfolder, and a build does not copy files from beside your map: a saved map has no folder to copy from, and a file build would then compile a map the compiler itself refuses where it lies. Put the file at the path the key's value gives, relative to the game directory, and build again.

roots.purpose: read the staged map source, write the BSP beside it, and hold the home directory Q3Map2 would otherwise take from the user
read the base game's shader scripts and textures, whose surfaceparms are baked into the BSP

actions.title: Compute visibility
actions.description:
The VIS stage rewrites the BSP it is given, and opens the `.prt` of the same stem beside it without being told to — which is why the portal file is an input here and is staged with the BSP.

`-saveprt` is not an option. Measured: without it Q3Map2 deletes the portal file when it finishes, and an action must not be able to destroy a file it was handed.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast, crude visibility
options.description: Upstream calls it very fast and crude. It is for looking at what you just built, not for what you ship.

options.name: mergeportals
options.title: Merge portals
options.description: Upstream: sometimes much faster, and usually does not hurt the frame rate.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: As for the compile stage: a name, not a path.

diagnostics.message: Q3Map2 could not open a file it needs — for this stage that is normally the portal file of the same name as the BSP.
diagnostics.hint: The compile stage produces it. A leaked map has none, because the compile stops before writing one.

diagnostics.message: The BSP has no portals, so there is nothing to compute.
diagnostics.hint: A map that is one open room has one cluster and no portals. That is not an error; it means visibility has nothing to cull.

diagnostics.message: Visibility data written.
Q3Map2 stopped with an error; its next line says which.

roots.purpose: rewrite the staged BSP with its visibility data
read the base game content Q3Map2 loads at startup
read your own content, which overlays the base game's

actions.title: Compute lighting
actions.description:
The LIGHT stage writes the lightmaps into the BSP. There is no separate lighting file: Quake III lightmaps live inside the BSP, or — for a build that asked for external ones, which this document does not — in a directory beside it.

It needs two companion files beside the BSP and refuses without either: `<stem>.srf`, which the compile stage wrote, and `<stem>.map`, the map source itself. Both are staged with the BSP. A lighting job that staged only the BSP would exit 1 saying a script file was not found, and the file it named would be one nobody thought they had asked for.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast lighting
options.description: Ignores tiny light contributions. Quick, and visibly rougher.

options.name: filter
options.title: Filter the lightmaps
options.description: Blurs the lightmap slightly, which hides sampling noise.

options.name: samples
options.title: Adaptive supersampling
options.description: Q3Map2's own `-samples`: how hard it works on the edges of shadows.

options.name: bounce
options.title: Radiosity bounces
options.description: How many times light bounces off surfaces. Each bounce costs another full pass.

options.name: shade
options.title: Phong shading
options.description: Smooths lighting across surfaces that meet at a shallow angle.

options.name: patchshadows
options.title: Shadows from patches
options.description: Patches do not cast shadows unless this is on; they always receive light, and the shadows brushes cast. Auto-Pigeon's light preview shows the default — no shadows cast by patches — and does not know this setting.

options.name: mod
options.title: Mod directory name
options.description: As for the compile stage: a name, not a path.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: Measured: this stage produces a different BSP on different runs above one thread, and the same one every time at one thread. Use one when you need to compare a build with the last one byte for byte.

diagnostics.match: was not found: No such file or directory
diagnostics.message: The lighting stage could not open a file it needs beside the BSP — the surface file the compile wrote, or the map source.
diagnostics.hint: Both are staged with the BSP by this profile. Seeing this means one of them was not produced by the compile stage.

diagnostics.message: A shader the map names has no image. Its flags are its script's if one defines it, Q3Map2's defaults if none does.
The lightmaps were packed and stored in the BSP.
